p: Modern PHP frameworks often use "magic" dependency injection, where scripts executed in a global scope or inside closures still have access to a fully initialized application instance via $this. However, IDEs like PhpStorm usually treat $this outside of classes as invalid or mixed, losing all type inference, autocompletion, and navigation.

Contextual This for PHP solves this problem by allowing you to map specific project directories to target PHP classes. Once configured, the plugin forces PhpStorm to recognize $this as an instance of your specified class inside those directories.

ul.li: Directory-to-Class Mapping: Map any number of directories (e.g., /content/, /routes/) to specific classes (e.g., \App\Kernel).
Full Autocompletion: Get method and property suggestions for $this-> as if you were inside the class itself.
Chained Method Resolution: Autocompletion works perfectly even for chains like $this->getRequest()->.
Closure Support: Works seamlessly inside global scopes and anonymous functions (closures).
Easy Configuration: Use the native IDE class picker to select your target classes and directories without typing FQNs manually.

ol.li: Open Settings (or Preferences) -> Tools -> Contextual This.
Click the + button to add a new mapping.
Select the directory (e.g., content/api) and the target PHP class (e.g., \MyApp\Kernel).
Click Apply and enjoy full IDE support for $this in your scripts!

p.i: Note: This plugin is designed for PHP frameworks that utilize this specific architectural pattern.
